errors.text: The hypothesis attributes segregation to strongly negative Au-Co and Au-Pt mixing enthalpies. Negative mixing enthalpy generally favors mixing, ordering, or intermetallic formation rather than phase separation, and the cited evidence does not establish these claimed thermochemical values for Au-Co-Cu-Ni-Pt nanoparticles.
It predicts Au/Pt surface enrichment, whereas the target mechanism is preferential Au/Cu surface segregation followed by melting and evaporation.

It identifies Ostwald ripening as the principal cause of small-particle loss, while the target attributes the loss and net size reduction primarily to segregation-assisted melting and evaporation of Au/Cu.
It predicts evolution toward faceted or irregular particles, contrary to the observed elliptical-to-spherical reshaping.
